clue.text: Selection from Italian designer's range

indicators.note: Selection from says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A fashion house in Milan picks a few pieces from its latest collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Range' reads as a designer's product line, but it is a mountain range, sitting inside italIAN DESigner's.
explanation.definitionFit: The Andes are the long mountain chain running down western South America, so they are a range.

clue.text: Awkward bum must head for bingo hall

indicators.note: bum as an adjective means bad or faulty, so these letters are messed up
head for picks the first letter of bingo

explanation.surface: A clumsy layabout heads off to the bingo hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bum' looks like the noun; it is the adjective meaning bad, rearranging MUST, B and HALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Being all thumbs is an idiom for clumsiness with the hands.

clue.text: Material is exploited, having turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry turned up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a resource that is mined is being exploited

explanation.surface: Fabric is used to full advantage once it arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: MINED read upwards in the grid gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is the sturdy cotton twill fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Time to stop representative figures making laws

indicators.note: to stop means the letter plugs a gap inside the other word

parts.note: statues are sculpted figures representing people

explanation.surface: It is time to end statues of public figures being made into law.
explanation.walkthrough: T stops a gap in STATUES.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutes are written laws passed by a legislature.

clue.text: Driving away fast, one avoided reversing first

indicators.note: first says the turned-round piece comes at the front, before the period of fasting
reversing tells us the word for someone shunned is read from its end back to its start

parts.note: a leper is the classic outcast, someone everyone avoids
Lent is the Christian season of fasting, so a fast

explanation.surface: A motorist speeds off, having swerved to miss someone before backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' looks like motoring and 'fast' like speed; LEPER read backwards gives REPEL, then LENT, the fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repellent drives others away, as an insect repellent keeps bugs off.

clue.text: Old car loses its initial value

indicators.note: loses its initial means the first letter of the word for the old car is dropped

parts.note: crate is slang for an old, battered car

explanation.surface: A classic car depreciates from its original price.
explanation.walkthrough: CRATE drops its first letter through 'loses its initial'.
explanation.definitionFit: To rate something is to value or assess it.

clue.text: Exceptional pressure of the joints

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for pressure in physics
articular is the medical adjective relating to joints

explanation.surface: A doctor notes unusual stress on the patient's joints.
explanation.definitionFit: Particular can mean special or out of the ordinary, as in 'of particular interest'.

clue.text: Raise the dough to quit before November

parts.note: to leave is to quit
N is November in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to earn money before leaving the job in November.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise the dough' sounds like making money; it is literal baking.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaven, as a verb, means add a raising agent such as yeast so bread rises.

clue.text: Attendants dashed out carrying incense? On the contrary

indicators.note: carrying says one piece is held inside another
On the contrary reverses the roles, so the word for incense holds the rearranged letters

parts.note: to incense someone is to enrage them

indicators.note: dashed means smashed, so the letters of out are rearranged

explanation.surface: Temple attendants rush out with incense burners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incense' is the verb, not the perfume. 'dashed' rearranges OUT to TOU, and 'On the contrary' flips 'carrying' so ENRAGE holds it.
explanation.definitionFit: An entourage is the group of attendants accompanying an important person.

clue.text: Roughly holding up end of elephant's trunk

indicators.note: in a down entry holding up means the second piece sits under the first, supporting it
end of picks the final letter of the animal's name

parts.note: or so means roughly, as in ten or so

explanation.surface: Roughly supporting the end of an elephant's trunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trunk' looks like the elephant's nose but means the body; T sits atop OR SO.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the human body's central part, also called the trunk.

clue.text: New players breaking real ground for City

indicators.note: breaking means the new players burst into the middle of the other letters
ground means crushed and broken up, so the word real is rearranged

parts.note: the players in a show are its cast

explanation.surface: Fresh signings break into the real ground of a city football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' looks like a football ground but rearranges REAL into LA..ER, which N and CAST break into.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancaster is a historic city in north-west England, the county town of Lancashire.

clue.text: Sign of hesitation after key change

indicators.note: after puts the hesitation sound behind the key, as the answer order needs

parts.note: Alt is a key on a computer keyboard
er is the sound people make when hesitating

explanation.surface: Someone pauses with an 'er' before a key change in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key change' reads as music, but the key is the ALT key on a keyboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To alter something is to modify it, the verb sense of change.

clue.text: Sweet smell associated with insect

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
a bug is an insect

explanation.surface: A sugary odour draws in a passing insect.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM for a stink is informal British usage. A humbug is a hard peppermint sweet popular in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A humbug is a striped boiled peppermint, a traditional British confection.

clue.text: Instruction to musicians playing trio to hold melody back?

indicators.note: to hold means the rearranged trio wraps around the other piece
playing suggests the letters of trio are performed in a new order
back tells us the word for a melody is turned around

parts.note: a tune is a melody

explanation.surface: A score tells a trio to hold back on the melody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges TRIO to RIT..O, which holds ENUT, TUNE read backwards through 'back'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ritenuto is an Italian score marking telling performers to slow down at once.

clue.text: At home, phoning about fellow trespassing

indicators.note: about here means next to or near, so the phoning piece is placed alongside the fellow

parts.note: in means at home
ringing means phoning

explanation.surface: Someone at home calls about a man who is on their land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' tempts you to put one piece around another, but here it just means alongside, so the pieces run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Infringing means encroaching on rights or territory, which is what trespassing does.

clue.text: Parent keeps naughty girl finally in line for many years

indicators.note: keeps means the parent holds the other letters inside

parts.note: mum is a mother, a parent

indicators.note: naughty suggests misbehaving letters, so these are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of girl

explanation.surface: A mother keeps her badly behaved daughter in line for years on end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naughty' rearranges its letters into ILLENNI; 'keeps' splits the parent word after its first letter to hold them.
explanation.definitionFit: A millennium is a span of a thousand years, which is certainly a great many.

clue.text: Gym relies on developing coastal town

indicators.note: developing means changing form, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: A gym's business depends on the town growing.
explanation.walkthrough: LYME REGIS is a seaside town in Dorset, southern England, famous for fossils.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyme Regis sits on the English Channel coast, on the Jurassic Coast.

clue.text: Help to give worker influence

definitions.meaning: a ... is assistance, as in lend a ...
a manual worker, as in farmhand
having a ... in something means having influence over it

explanation.surface: Assisting someone means giving a labourer some sway.
explanation.walkthrough: Four separate meanings of the one short word sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Hand covers assistance, passing over, a labourer and a share of control in everyday idioms.

clue.text: Briefly, did fruit containing juice die out?

indicators.note: containing means the pair of pieces holds the juice between them
briefly means the word is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: taken as written before it is shortened
a pear is a fruit
sap is the juice of a plant

explanation.surface: Asking whether a juicy fruit species became extinct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' drops the final letter; 'containing' has the two outer pieces together hold the juice between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To disappear can mean to cease to exist, as a species dies out.

clue.text: Transport barrels out of plant

indicators.note: out of means the barrels are taken away from the plant

parts.note: euphorbia is a genus of plants, the spurges
B is an abbreviation for barrel

explanation.surface: Shipping barrels out of a factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' looks like shipping but means ecstasy; 'plant' is a botanical plant, not a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport can mean overwhelming joy, as in transports of delight, which is euphoria.

clue.text: A little problem? So we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells us the answer is spoken the same as a word for a problem

parts.note: a sum is an arithmetic problem

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether there is a slight problem, and is told so.
explanation.walkthrough: SUM, an arithmetic problem, is pronounced the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Some means a modest amount, as in 'have some cake'.

clue.text: Arrest involved capturing certain people handling money

indicators.note: capturing means the rearranged letters close around the other word
involved means tangled up, so the letters of arrest are rearranged

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: An arrest of certain cash handlers, perhaps for embezzlement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges ARREST to TREA..RS, which captures SURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasurers manage the funds of a club, company or government.

clue.text: Old country hotel surrounded by suspicion

indicators.note: surrounded by means the letter for hotel sits inside the other word

parts.note: a suspicion is a trace, as in a suspicion of garlic
H is hotel in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: An old country hotel is under a cloud of suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspicion' means a hint or touch here, TRACE.
explanation.definitionFit: Thrace was an ancient region of south-east Europe.

clue.text: French sea song required for commercial

parts.note: mer is the French word for sea
a chant is a simple song

explanation.surface: A French sea shanty is needed for an advertisement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'commercial' reads as an advert, but it is the adjective, as in merchant shipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Merchant as an adjective means trading or commercial, as in merchant navy or merchant bank.

clue.text: Following fashion, Mike gets computer device

indicators.note: following puts the radio letter after the word for fashion

parts.note: mode means fashion, as in a la mode
M is Mike in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A trendy man called Mike buys a gadget.
explanation.definitionFit: A modem is the box linking a computer to a phone or cable network.

clue.text: Be sparing with hot, not cold, seafood

indicators.note: with hot, not cold says one letter is put in where the other one stood

parts.note: to scrimp is to be sparing or economical
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A diner is told to go easy on hot dishes and serve seafood chilled instead.
explanation.walkthrough: C and H are the cold and hot markings on taps; H takes C's place in SCRIMP.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrimps are small crustaceans eaten as seafood.

clue.text: Flipping old bore, I state

indicators.note: flipping means turning over, so the pieces are read upwards

parts.note: had is a past tense like bore, as in bore or had a child

explanation.surface: An exasperated person declares themselves a flipping old bore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British curse; it reverses O, HAD and I. 'bore' is the verb, not a dull person.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a state in the north-western United States.

clue.text: European bound by rail for Paddington?

indicators.note: bound by means the letter is enclosed within the other word

parts.note: a bar is a rail

explanation.surface: A European traveller kept in by the railings at Paddington station.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paddington' and 'rail' suggest the London station; it is the children's book bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Paddington is the marmalade-loving bear of Michael Bond's books, an example signalled by the question mark.

clue.text: Opinion of boxer, perhaps Muhammad Ali originally

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog, so a dog by example

indicators.note: originally picks the opening letters of the boxer's two names

explanation.surface: Asking what view a famous boxer like Muhammad Ali held.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxer' points to Ali, but it is the breed of dog; Muhammad Ali gives only MA.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is a firmly held belief or doctrine, a fixed opinion.

clue.text: Brew a beer in it and get drunk

indicators.note: brew means stir and mix up, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Home brewing instructions that end with getting tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' is the noun: an inebriate is a habitual drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun an inebriate is a drunkard, someone habitually intoxicated.

clue.text: Runner turned green after hash

indicators.note: after sends the rearranged colour behind the word for a hash, reversing the clue order

parts.note: a hash is a mess, as in make a hash of something

indicators.note: turned means the letters of green are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone goes pale green after eating hash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives ENGER; 'Runner' is an errand-runner, not an athlete.
explanation.definitionFit: A messenger carries notes or errands, so a runner in the old office sense.

clue.text: Loved one needs protection? Not right

indicators.note: not means the letter for right is dropped from the word

parts.note: armour is protective covering

explanation.surface: A sweetheart may need shielding, though not on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: ARMOUR loses its R through 'Not right'.
explanation.definitionFit: Amour can mean a lover or love affair, borrowed from French for love.
